notes: Read all 107 source lines (numbered) before editing. The web hook installs a global `keydown` listener on `window` to implement: a form-field guard, a '?' cheat-sheet toggle, a Ctrl/⌘+K or '/' command-palette open (via `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('toggle-command-palette'))`), and a two-stroke 'g then <key>' GOTO navigation mode driven by react-router-dom's `useNavigate()`. The window keydown listener, the `KeyboardEvent`/`HTMLElement` DOM types, the `CustomEvent` dispatch and `useNavigate()` are all browser-only — no React Native analog (a native binary has no hardware-keyboard keydown stream and no react-router). Ported faithfully behind native-safe facades + injected callbacks per the useFaviconBadge ('prefer globalThis.* when present, else explicit unavailable state') and LegacyAlertRulesRedirect/Breadcrumbs/App.tsx ('onNavigate(path) callback replaces react-router') conventions.

L1 `import { useEffect, useState, useCallback, useRef } from 'react'` -> `import {useCallback, useEffect, useRef, useState} from 'react'` (react is RN-compatible; native prettier drops inner-brace spacing and sorts named imports; all four hooks still imported and used).

L2 `import { useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom'` REMOVED — react-router-dom is browser-only and not a native dependency. Its single use (`navigate(shortcut.path)`) is replaced by an injected `onNavigate?: (path: string) => void` callback on the new optional `UseKeyboardShortcutsOptions` arg (the same `onNavigate(path)` precedent used by the ported App.tsx / Breadcrumbs / LegacyAlertRulesRedirect). reactRouterNavigateAvailable: false is recorded in nativeKeyboardShortcutsCapabilities.

L4 `type ShortcutMode = 'idle' | 'goto'` ported verbatim. L6-10 `interface ShortcutState { mode; showCheatSheet; toggleCheatSheet }` ported verbatim and kept unexported, matching the web export surface exactly (it is referenced only as the hook's return annotation).

L12-28 GOTO_SHORTCUTS ported byte-for-byte: same `export const`, same `Record<string, {path: string; label: string}>` type, all 14 entries with identical paths and labels (d:/ Dashboard, v:/vehicles Vehicles, c:/charging Charging, r:/drives Drives, t:/trips Trips, b:/battery 'Battery & Energy', a:/analytics Analytics, e:/efficiency Efficiency, s:/settings Settings, n:/notifications/inbox Notifications, l:/live-signals 'Live Signals', o:/automations Automations, x:/commands Commands, i:/climate Climate). The single-char keys are written unquoted (d:) per native prettier `quoteProps:'as-needed'`; identical at runtime to the web quoted ('d':) form. JSDoc 'Navigation shortcuts activated by pressing g then a target key' (L12) preserved. API path intent preserved exactly.

L30 `const GOTO_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500` ported verbatim. Added a module-local `COMMAND_PALETTE_EVENT = 'toggle-command-palette'` constant capturing the exact event name the web L74 dispatches, so the react-native-web fallback dispatch stays byte-for-byte interoperable with the web shell's listener.

Browser-only DOM types replaced by native-safe facade interfaces (RN tsconfig lib excludes `dom`): web's `KeyboardEvent` -> KeyboardEventLike {key; ctrlKey; metaKey; target: KeyboardTargetLike | null; preventDefault()}; web's `HTMLElement` (`e.target as HTMLElement`) -> KeyboardTargetLike {tagName?: string; isContentEditable?: boolean}; `CustomEvent` -> CustomEventLike + CustomEventConstructor; the `window` event target -> KeyboardEventTargetLike {addEventListener('keydown'); removeEventListener('keydown'); dispatchEvent?}. All reached via `globalThis` casts so the real browser objects satisfy them on react-native-web.

L33 `const navigate = useNavigate()` -> destructured `const {onNavigate, onToggleCommandPalette} = options` (the native-safe injected replacements; see L2 note). L34 `useState<ShortcutMode>('idle')` (mode/setMode) ported verbatim. L35 `useState(false)` (showCheatSheet/setShowCheatSheet) ported verbatim. L36 `const timeoutRef = useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout>>()` -> `useRef<ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined>(undefined)` (React 19's `@types/react` dropped the zero-argument `useRef` overload, requiring an explicit `undefined` initial value; behaviour-identical — the ref still starts undefined and holds the pending timeout handle; setTimeout/clearTimeout exist in RN).

All four web `clearTimeout(timeoutRef.current)` calls (Escape L67, GOTO-enter L81, GOTO-target L94, cleanup L102) are routed through a new module-scoped `clearPendingTimeout(handle)` helper that guards `handle !== undefined` before calling `clearTimeout`. React Native's typings declare `clearTimeout(handle: number)` with a required argument (the browser DOM lib's is optional), so passing the `number | undefined` ref directly fails tsc; the guard is a no-op when no GOTO timeout is pending — byte-for-byte the web `clearTimeout(undefined)` semantics — and keeps the four call sites DRY.
L38-40 `toggleCheatSheet = useCallback(() => setShowCheatSheet(prev => !prev), [])` ported verbatim (arrow `prev => !prev` already paren-free, satisfies native arrowParens:'avoid').

L42-104 main `useEffect` ported. Web L42 assumes `window` is always present; native gates on it: `const eventTarget = getKeyboardEventTarget(); if (!eventTarget) return;` — getKeyboardEventTarget() returns react-native-web's `globalThis.window` when it exposes `addEventListener` and undefined on a pure native runtime (the inert no-op = faithful 'no hardware keyboard' outcome; hardwareKeyboardListeningAvailable: false). The web `window` variable is renamed `eventTarget` so the inner DOM node keeps the web's `target` variable name (L44).

L43-52 handler signature + form-field guard ported 1:1: `(e: KeyboardEvent)` -> `(e: KeyboardEventLike)` (parens kept — typed single param); web `const target = e.target as HTMLElement` -> `const target = e.target` (typed KeyboardTargetLike | null); the INPUT/TEXTAREA/SELECT/`isContentEditable` early-return guard preserved verbatim with `?.` added (target may be null) — behaviour-identical for real keydown targets which always exist.

L71-76 Ctrl+K (`e.key === 'k' && isCtrlOrMeta`) OR ('/' && !ctrlMeta && mode==='idle') -> `e.preventDefault()` then the command-palette toggle. Web's `window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('toggle-command-palette'))` is preserved as: prefer the injected `onToggleCommandPalette()` callback; when absent, fall back to `dispatchCommandPaletteToggle(eventTarget)` which dispatches `new CustomEvent('toggle-command-palette')` on the window facade when a real `dispatchEvent` + `CustomEvent` exist (react-native-web), exactly mirroring web. commandPaletteWindowEventAvailable: false documents the pure-native runtime. The long `||` condition is prettier-wrapped; logic unchanged.

L86-96 GOTO-target handling -> `GOTO_SHORTCUTS[e.key.toLowerCase()]`, on hit `e.preventDefault(); navigate(shortcut.path)` -> `onNavigate?.(shortcut.path)`, then setMode('idle') + clearTimeout regardless — ported verbatim with comment.

L99-103 `window.addEventListener('keydown', handler)` + cleanup (`removeEventListener` + `clearTimeout(timeoutRef.current)`) ported 1:1 against `eventTarget`. L104 dependency array `[mode, navigate, toggleCheatSheet]` -> `[mode, onNavigate, onToggleCommandPalette, toggleCheatSheet]` (navigate replaced by the two injected callbacks it superseded; mode + toggleCheatSheet unchanged; satisfies react-hooks/exhaustive-deps).
L106-107 `return { mode, showCheatSheet, toggleCheatSheet }` ported verbatim (no inner-brace spaces per native prettier). The return contract / state names are byte-for-byte identical to web.

Browser unavailability made explicit via exported `nativeKeyboardShortcutsCapabilities` {hardwareKeyboardListeningAvailable:false, reactRouterNavigateAvailable:false, commandPaletteWindowEventAvailable:false}; the full keydown + dispatch path still executes on the react-native-web target where a real `window`/`CustomEvent` exist, so genuine parity is retained there. No DOM elements, Recharts, Leaflet, react-router-dom, or web UI components are imported; the only runtime dependency is react.

Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck (tsc --noEmit); npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles. No existing test imports this hook; typecheck + lint cover the new module.
